---
title: "Reproduce"
---

## Environment

```bash
git clone git@github.com:Manish-Bilore/mumbai-anthropogenic-heat.git
cd mumbai-anthropogenic-heat
conda env create -f environment.yml
conda activate mumbaiqf
```

NumPy is pinned below 2.0: several compiled dependencies in the geospatial stack are built
against the 1.x ABI.

## Inputs

Place in `data/raw/` (see [Data](data.qmd) for sources):

`buildings.gpkg`, `mumbai_typology.gpkg`, `wards.gpkg`,
`mumbai_ward_population_bmc.csv`, `mapped_slums_2016.kml`,
`mumbai_daily_temperature_1951_2024.csv`, `rr_localities.csv`

## Pipeline

```bash
python scripts/00a_normalise_ward_population.py       # BMC export -> schema
python scripts/00b_normalise_inputs.py                # wards, buildings, typology
python scripts/00c_make_typical_day.py --from-year 2020
python scripts/08_build_income_proxy.py               # ASR localities -> ward medians
python scripts/01_prepare_stock.py                    # floors, area, archetype, ward
python scripts/02_assign_population.py                # households, income band
python scripts/03_run_loads.py                        # hourly loads + waste heat
python scripts/04_gridify.py                          # 100 m grid + metabolism + traffic
python scripts/06_benchmark.py                        # vs Sailor et al.
python scripts/10_abm_ensemble.py --replicates 3      # the ABM
python scripts/11_morris_screening.py --trajectories 2
python scripts/12_export_web_series.py                # web/series.json
```

Then the map tiles (needs `tippecanoe`):

```bash
tippecanoe -o web/tiles/qf_years.pmtiles -l qf_years -Z 9 -z 14 \
  --no-feature-limit --no-tile-size-limit --force \
  data/processed/qf_grid_years.geojson
```

Preview locally with a server that honours HTTP Range requests — `python -m http.server`
does not, and PMTiles will silently fail:

```bash
cd web && python -m RangeHTTPServer 8000
```

## Everything is in one file

`config/params.yaml` holds every parameter, tagged `[placeholder]`, `[literature]` or
`[official]`. Nothing numeric is hardcoded in the modules. The file's hash is written into
every log line, so any result traces back to the exact parameter set that produced it.

## Runtimes

Measured on a laptop, 580,890 buildings:

| step | time |
|---|---|
| stock, population | ~30 s |
| loads + grid | ~1 min |
| ABM, 3 replicates | ~5 min |
| Morris, r = 2 (18 evaluations) | ~11 min |
| tiling | ~2 min |

## Building this site

```bash
quarto render          # -> docs/, copies web/ into docs/map/
```

GitHub Pages serves `docs/` from `main`.
